Contributions.We make three contributions.
• We argue for a compute-aware memory plane as a missing systems abstraction for
lifelong agents, and define memory capsules as its correction-aware core unit.
• We present an executable vLLM-first prototype that already demonstrates
correction-aware control-plane behavior through persistent capsule state,
concurrency-safe invalidation, an OpenAI-compatible sidecar, a typed serving
contract, and a live benchmark harness.
• We define a replay-and-placement policy, together with an explicit systems agenda
for deeper integration, that trades off semantic value, latency, staleness risk, and
locality across text retrieval and KV replay while leaving layer replay as future
engine work rather than a claimed implementation result.

evidence.excerpt:
A memory capsule is a versioned record with required semantic fields such as tenant identity,
surface text, timestamps, and validity windows, together with optional enrichment such as
summaries, provenance, entities, facts, dependencies, and artifact locators. The crucial step
is that a capsule can also name reusable runtime artifacts such as embeddings, KV cache
segments, and optional layer-frontier checkpoints.
This design gives one identifier for meaning and compute. A retriever can therefore answer
not onlywhich memory is relevant, but alsowhich reusable state is compatible and cheap to consume
on a specific node. In the current prototype, text and KV-aware routing are fully wired end to
end, while layer-frontier replay remains an explicit contract for future engine extensions.

evidence.excerpt:
For each request, PLACEMEMranks replay options across prompt-level text retrieval, KV
replay, and prospective layer replay. The policy evaluates a capsule c on target t under
replay moderwith a utility function of the form
U(c,t,r) =w 1Preuse +w 2Csaved +w 3Vsem −w 4Rstale −w 5Bremote −w 6Ltarget. (1)
Here, Preuse estimates near-term reuse, Csaved measures avoided prefill work, Vsem captures
task relevance, Rstale captures freshness risk, Bremote estimates transfer cost, and Ltarget
penalizes latency-sensitive targets. The selected decision is then turned into backend
metadata for the serving layer.
This differs from a local prefix cache in two ways. First, the decision is made in a control
plane rather than inside a single worker. Second, the decision is conditioned on semantic
validity and locality, not only on byte reuse. In other words, PLACEMEMtreats memory
reuse as a policy

evidence.excerpt:
uses a controlled task: each scenario has a structured canonical
identifier injected into the active capsule summary, and accuracy measures whether the live
model's response contains the post-correction identifier rather than the stale one, isolating
whether the control plane forwards the right summary rather than testing open-ended gen-
eration quality. The three-condition comparison shows why invalidation matters: without it
the control plane selects the stale capsule after a correction event, the model receives the
outdated summary, and post-correction accuracy drops to zero. Full PLACEMEMeliminates
stale selection while matching the TTFT of the reuse-without-invalidation condition (20.54
ms versus 20.73 ms), confirming that correction-aware control adds faithfulness at no la-
tency cost. The text-summary baseline reaches full accuracy but at 36.08 ms mean TTFT, a
75% overhead

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline outcomes are established by objective system measurements (TTFT, KV reuse rate, invalidation overhead) and exact-match canonical identifier checks on a live vLLM backend, which do not depend on the rule-based routing and invalidation policies under study.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective runtime metrics (mean TTFT, KV reuse rate, invalidation latency) and exact-match post-correction identifier accuracy from live model outputs.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Rule-based replay utility scoring and deterministic dependency-graph invalidation mechanisms in the control plane.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The claims are well calibrated: the paper explicitly frames layer-frontier replay and multi-node heterogeneous placement as future agenda items while presenting empirical results strictly for the control plane and KV routing/invalidation prototype.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation carefully scopes claims by assessing control-plane routing, latency (TTFT), KV reuse, and post-correction accuracy across a 48-turn mock streaming trace and a live vLLM backend using a small model (LFM2.5-230M) across 27 post-correction queries and a 340-turn benchmark.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on objective system runtime measurements (TTFT in milliseconds) and objective substring verification of canonical identifiers on a live vLLM serving backend.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: System metrics (mean TTFT, KV reuse rate, invalidation latency) and exact-match post-correction identifier accuracy from model outputs.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Rule-based routing policies and deterministic dependency-graph invalidation mechanisms designed into the control plane.

primary.limitations: The prototype relies on a sidecar rather than deep engine modifications, and testing is limited to small-scale pilot traces and a 230M-parameter model rather than full production clusters.
primary.method_assessment: The architecture introduces a capsule schema, catalog, dependency graph, admission shim, and an OpenAI-compatible routing sidecar interacting with vLLM backends, supported by an explicit replay utility formulation.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript offers a clean, well-bounded systems contribution addressing the mismatch between lifelong agent semantic memory updates and serving-engine runtime cache staleness, supported by reproducible architecture details and transparent pilot benchmarks.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper contributes a systems architecture and executable control-plane prototype (PLACEMEM) for lifelong LLM agents, introducing 'memory capsules' that bind semantic memory records to reusable runtime compute state (KV caches) with dependency-tracked cascading invalidation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript offers a clean, well-bounded systems contribution addressing the mismatch between lifelong agent semantic memory updates and serving-engine runtime cache staleness, supported by reproducible architecture details and transparent pilot benchmarks.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The prototype relies on a sidecar rather than deep engine modifications, and testing is limited to small-scale pilot traces and a 230M-parameter model rather than full production clusters.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
